title: Operator Dashboard: Scaling Playback with Annotated Change History
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: ship a consolidated Operator Dashboard feature that lets operators replay fleet scaling decisions (scaling playback), inspect annotated change history with human/operator notes, and correlate those events against real throughput and latency signals. This is targeting Dedicated capacity customers who need auditability for autoscale decisions and a compact troubleshooting surface for production incidents. Scope includes: 1) UI timeline playback with pause/seek and speed controls; 2) annotated event detail panel (who/what/why + diff of target vs actual capacity); 3) linked telemetry graphs for throughput (RPS), p50/p95 latency, and provision latency; 4) event filters and export (CSV/PDF); 5) retention controls for change history and UX for operators to add notes during playback. Out of scope: changes to autoscaler algorithms themselves and multi-fleet cross-correlation in this sprint.
acceptance_criteria: Timeline view displays scaling events in chronological order with visual markers for manual overrides, autoscaler triggers, and fallback events.
Playback controls allow play/pause, step-forward/backward by event, and adjustable playback speed up to 4x.
Selecting an event opens an annotated detail panel showing timestamp, actor (user or system), reason, pre/post capacity, related PR or runbook links, and operator notes.
Telemetry panel plots actual throughput (RPS), p50/p95 latency, queue length, and provision latency aligned with the timeline; graphs support zoom to event.
Operators can add/edit notes on events; edits are appended to audit trail with user and timestamp.
Change history export produces a CSV with events, annotations, and delta fields and respects the fleet's retention policy.
Backend APIs (GET /fleets/{id}/scaling-events and GET /fleets/{id}/telemetry) return payloads within 250ms p95 for 30-day ranges for a typical fleet.
Feature gated behind console-2025.03 release flag and available to Dedicated customers only.
E2E QA verifies that manual override events result in corresponding timeline markers and that rollback events are visible and annotated.

notes: Implementation plan: 1) Backend: extend scaling-events API to include actor, reason_detail, annotations array, and telemetry window (ENG-62011, ENG-62990). 2) Frontend: implement timeline component with virtualized rendering for large event sets; playback engine will request telemetry windows on-demand and cache. 3) Storage/Retention: reuse existing audit store with retention param (default 180d); provide admin override in fleet settings. 4) Rollout: behind feature flag, enable for 10 early adopter customers, collect feedback for 2 weeks, then broader rollout. Operational runbook will include a diagnostic mode to capture missing telemetry linkages.
dashboard_queries: SELECT timestamp, event_type, actor, reason, previous_capacity, target_capacity, actual_capacity FROM fleet_scaling_events WHERE fleet_id = $fleet_id ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1000
SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) as minute, avg(rps) as rps FROM fleet_telemetry WHERE fleet_id = $fleet_id AND ts BETWEEN $start AND $end GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute
SELECT event_id, jsonb_array_length(annotations) as annotation_count FROM fleet_scaling_events WHERE fleet_id = $fleet_id ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 500
qa_checklist: Validate timeline displays and event ordering across time zones
Play/pause/seek behave deterministically and do not skip events under load
Event detail shows linked artifacts (PR/runbook) when provided
Annotation create/edit appends audit entry and is immutable aside from appended edit comment
Export CSV matches visible filtered set and includes telemetry aggregates
Feature flag gating prevents access for non-Dedicated customers
Verify API performance targets in staging for 7/14/30 day windows
